name: Commercial Christmas Trees
headline: Trees sized for plazas, not living rooms.
summary: Freestanding commercial Christmas trees from 8 to 30 feet — sectional steel frames, pre-strung commercial LED and anchoring engineered for exposed sites.
intro: A commercial tree has to do two jobs a retail tree never does: survive a season of open weather, and read from the far side of a parking lot. Ours are built on bolt-together steel frames, pre-strung with commercial-grade LED, and anchored with ballast plates or guy-wire rated for the wind exposure of the actual site. The 14-foot is the size most courtyards and entrances land on; past about 20 feet you are into civic-square territory.

name: Giant Trees
headline: 30 feet and up, for civic squares.
summary: Landmark-scale trees from 30 to 100 feet — engineered structures with lift-assisted installation, for downtown cores, malls and municipal squares.
intro: Past 30 feet a Christmas tree stops being décor and becomes a structure. These are engineered installations: a steel armature, a documented anchoring plan, lift-assisted assembly and a power distribution design. They are what a downtown BIA puts at the centre of a tree-lighting event, and they are specified around sightlines, crowd flow and how the square is used the rest of the year.

name: Wreaths, Garland & Pole Décor
headline: 4-foot wreaths built for building fronts.
summary: Commercial wreaths from 3 to 8 feet, matching garland runs, and pole wraps that turn a whole street into one continuous display.
intro: A residential wreath disappears on a commercial facade — from the parking lot it reads as a smudge. Four feet is the smallest size that holds a standard commercial entrance, which is why it is the one we specify most. Garland and pole wraps are what tie it together: once the light standards down a street are wrapped, the individual decorations stop reading as separate objects and the street reads as decorated.

name: Snowflakes & Pole Motifs
headline: Light the whole street, not one building.
summary: Pole-mounted LED snowflakes, stars, bells and bespoke motifs — the fastest way to make a downtown core read as decorated end to end.
intro: Pole motifs are the highest-impact spend in commercial holiday décor. One decoration on one building is an ornament; the same budget spread across twenty light standards is a destination. Ours are aluminum-framed, commercially lit, and built with the bracket hardware to mount on standard municipal poles. Designs run from classic snowflakes through to bespoke shapes cut to a BIA's own brand.

name: Giant Ornaments
headline: Ornaments people stand next to for photos.
summary: Oversized shatterproof ornaments from 2 to 10 feet — ground-set clusters, suspended installations and stacked centrepieces.
intro: Giant ornaments do something a tree cannot: they work at ground level, where people walk. Set a cluster at an entrance and it becomes the photo people take. They ship as shatterproof shells with a weighted or staked base, in stock colours or matched to a property's palette, and they scale from a 2-foot accent up to a 10-foot centrepiece.

name: Holiday Displays
headline: Stars, orbs and light sculpture.
summary: Illuminated stars, orb clusters, ice-shard forms and walk-through pieces — sculptural lighting that turns a property into somewhere people go.
intro: Rooflines make a property look decorated. Displays make people drive to it. This range is the sculptural end of the catalogue: dimensional stars that hang over a street, orb clusters scattered across a lawn, faceted ice-shard forms, and walk-through pieces built to be photographed. They are commercial-grade steel and LED, designed to stand outside all season and to be re-installed year after year.

name: Topiaries
headline: Sculpted figures that stay all year.
summary: Artificial topiary animals and forms — a year-round installation that carries a property through the seasons, not just December.
intro: Topiaries are the piece of the catalogue that is not really about Christmas. They are artificial, UV-stable sculpted forms — animals, spirals, cones and columns — that stay on a property through the year and can be dressed seasonally. For clients who want the decorating budget to work more than six weeks a year, this is usually where that conversation starts.

name: Botanical Gardens
headline: Ticketed light experiences.
summary: Sculptural lighting and immersive installations designed for botanical gardens, conservatories and ticketed winter light walks.
intro: A garden light walk is a different brief again: the visitor is moving through the installation rather than driving past it, the route has to build, and everything has to work around living collections. We design these as a sequence — arrival, set pieces, quieter stretches, a finale — with lighting that respects the planting and hardware that installs without damaging root zones or beds.
